newsitem.title: USA: Tornadoes hit central Tennessee, at least 15 hurt.
newsitem.headline: Tornadoes hit central Tennessee, at least 15 hurt.

text.p: A series of tornadoes skipped through central Tennessee on Friday, ripping the roof off a grocery store, rupturing gas lines and trapping some people inside damaged homes, authorities said.
At least 15 people were treated in a hospital in Murfreesboro, about 30 miles (50 km) south of Nashville, for injuries ranging from mild to serious, authorities said.
Rescue crews were working to free people from damaged buildings in the nearby Barfield area of Rutherford County.

"So far we have had no confirmed fatalities, which is fantastic considering the velocity of these storms and the speed with which they moved through," said Cecil Whaley, head of the Tennessee Emergency Management Agency.

Electric power was reported to be out in Smyrna, site of a large Nissan plant, and homeward-bound motorists were caught in huge traffic jams. The roof was blown off a Food Lion grocery store in Smyrna, but no customers were injured.
"We have broken gas lines to contend with, to avoid secondary explosions from that," Whaley said.
The tornadoes also rolled through Wilson, Lincoln and Bedford counties in central Tennessee, he said.
"It's spread out all over middle Tennessee, and it's still dangerous," he said of the storm.
